note: Census's own cautions about comparing particular measures across particular ACS periods. A note applies to a change map when the measure matches and either period contains one of the listed years. Shown under the change legend; listed in the data dictionary.

notes.text: The 2008 ACS changed the labor-force questions; Census recommends caution comparing data that include 2006–2007 responses with later data.
notes.source: Understanding and Using ACS Data (Census, 2020), ch. 4

notes.text: The educational-attainment question changed in 2008; Census flags education for caution when comparing 2006–10 with later periods.
The property-value question changed in 2008, which Census says may have caused an inconsistency with earlier values.

From the 2018–22 release on, Census reports home values in the final year's dollars; earlier periods are reported values without adjustment. STRATA's factor uses average prices over pooled periods, but changes across that boundary mix the two conventions.
Census flags language for caution in comparisons with 2006–10 (the 'linguistically isolated' table was renamed, with the same definition).
Census flags race and Hispanic origin for caution in comparisons with 2006–10.
Periods that include 2020–2022 contain pandemic-era commuting; working from home and transit use shifted sharply.
The 2019 questionnaire split rail categories; the public-transportation total remains comparable.
notes.source: ACS 2019 Subject Definitions, Means of Transportation

notes.text: Census asks for caution comparing periods that include 2020: the pandemic disrupted collection and Census changed its nonresponse weighting.
